I'm 12 years and 8 months old, with a body mass index of 16.9. I'm female and 148 centimeters tall, weighing 37 kilograms. I was hospitalized for three days. My doctors calculated my Alvarado score as 4 and my pediatric appendicitis score as 3. An ultrasound examination revealed that my appendix measured 7.1 millimeters in diameter. I experienced pain in my lower right abdomen, which I described as a migratory pain, and had tenderness on the opposite side of my body when I pressed, but not when I coughed. I also felt unwell, had no appetite, and my temperature was normal at 37 degrees Celsius. Laboratory tests showed 7.7 white blood cells per microliter, but no signs of an infection in my blood. My red blood cell count was normal, but my CRP level was zero. Urinalysis results showed that I had ketones and a small amount of blood in my urine, but no white blood cells. I didn't have any difficulty urinating and my bowel movements were normal. However, I had a positive psoas sign, meaning that my doctor could press on a specific point in my lower back and cause me pain. An ultrasound of my abdomen revealed that there was no free fluid, my appendix wall was intact, and it showed signs of being inflamed, suggesting that I might have an appendicolith. Surrounding tissue was reacting to the inflammation, but there was no sign of a perforation or an abscess. My lymph nodes were swollen, but there were no signs of enteritis, bowel obstruction, or other complications. My treatment plan was conservative, as my condition was considered uncomplicated.
